SMTO-FIL-0008 — SMTO couldn't use the file name pattern it was given

GUID: 00b1f143-5edf-468f-bb5d-64cf602ead8c
Slug: file-invalid-glob
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO tried to pick out files with a name pattern (like *.csv) that it couldn't read, so the search or listing didn't run. No files were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, describe the files you want in plain words, for example "all .csv files in the reports folder", and ask SMTO to try again. SMTO writes the pattern itself, and a clear description helps it write one it can use.
  2. If you typed a pattern yourself, use forward slashes (/) between folder names, not backslashes (), and close every [ with a ]. Backslashes and an unclosed [ are the usual reasons this pattern is refused.
  3. Keep the pattern short and simple. Use ** only when you mean "in any folder below this one". Very long patterns (over 4,096 characters) are refused before any file is looked at.

What success looks like

  • SMTO lists or finds the files you expected, and this message doesn't appear again.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details in this panel and send them, together with a description of the files you wanted, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep sending the same pattern unchanged; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway file walker rejected a glob pattern because it contains a backslash or NUL character, exceeds 4096 characters, or has an unclosed [ character class.

What this means

  • Glob compilation rejected backslashes, NUL, more than 4096 characters or an unterminated bracket expression. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Glob compilation rejected backslashes, NUL, more than 4096 characters or an unterminated bracket expression.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the glob's separators, brackets and length; glob syntax is different from regular expressions.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the rejected pattern in the receipt (error_kind invalid_glob). Use '/'-separated portable segments with '**' for recursive matching, no backslashes or NUL, at most 4096 characters, and close every bracket expression (gateway_core/file_walk.glob_regex).
  • Correct the glob syntax shown by the safe validation field.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported bounded glob selects the intended paths.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
